 Agricultural losses from typhoon reach NT$221.63m
 By Yang Yuan-ting / 
Staff reporter, with CNA 
 Add TT as Preferred Source 
 Agricultural losses caused by Typhoon Champi had reached NT$221.63 million (US$6.82 million) as of 11am yesterday, with garlic crops sustaining the heaviest damage, the Ministry of Agriculture said.
 Crop losses accounted for NT$210.73 million, while livestock losses, primarily pigs, stood at NT$90,000, data compiled from local government reports by the ministry’s Agriculture and Food Agency and Department of Animal Industry showed.
 Damage to private facilities reached NT$10.8 million, which included NT$8.57 million in livestock and poultry facilities and NT$2.23 million in agricultural infrastructure, such as horizontal trellises and plastic greenhouses, the ministry said.
 Wind-damaged crops are pictured in Yunlin County yesterday after being battered by Typhoon Champi over the weekend.
 Photo: Huang Shu-li, Taipei Times
 Among crops, garlic sustained the most severe damage, with losses totaling NT$63.59 million.
 Other heavily affected crops included peanuts (NT$15.91 million), onions (NT$11.65 million), tangerines (NT$11.51 million) and corn (NT$9.99 million).
 By region, Yunlin County reported the heaviest agricultural losses at NT$137.07 million.
 It was followed by Miaoli County (NT$24.83 million), Taichung (NT$20.42 million), New Taipei City (NT$16.18 million) and Yilan County (NT$9.38 million).
 To mitigate the financial impact, the ministry announced cash relief and low-interest loans for nine municipalities: New Taipei City, Taoyuan and Taichung, as well as Changhua, Nantou, Yunlin, Yilan and Taitung counties.
 The subsidies cover crops, forestry, fisheries and livestock, the ministry said, adding that all agricultural products in Yilan County are eligible for the relief program.
 The relief package also includes items that did not strictly meet weather parameter thresholds, but were confirmed to have sustained severe damage during on-site inspections, it said.

 Starbucks Taiwan’s decision to charge for drink customization, which had been free, has sparked consumer backlash, highlighting the challenge of raising prices without making customers feel they are losing value, experts said.

Topping off drinks without ice was previously free, and disgruntled customers posted photos on social media showing that iced drinks ordered without ice were only half full if the extra NT$15 was not paid.

 A sea warning for Typhoon Champi might be issued tonight, while the storm’s trajectory would determine whether a land warning is to be issued tomorrow night, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said yesterday. 
As of 2pm yesterday, Champi was about 1,536km east-southeast of Taiwan proper’s southernmost point, Oluanpi (鵝鑾鼻), packing maximum sustained winds of 198kph, CWA forecaster Tseng Chao-cheng (曾昭誠) said. 
The storm was moving west-northwest at 23kph and was expected to strengthen over the next 24 hours before weakening slightly as it approaches cooler waters east of Taiwan, Tseng said.

 Donated vessel will not patrol waters near Taiwan: premier
 2026-10-21 
 A patrol vessel donated by the Coast Guard Administration (CGA) to the Philippines would not be used in waters near Taiwan or areas where Taiwanese fishing vessels operate, Premier Cho Jung-tai (卓榮泰) said yesterday.
The vessel, formerly the CGA's 500-tonne-class Kinmen (金門), was commissioned into the Philippine Coast Guard on Oct. 2.
Speaking at the Legislative Yuan, Cho said the Philippines had pledged during the donation process that the vessel would be used only for designated missions and would not operate in waters related to Taiwan. 
The vessel could even provide assistance to Taiwan if needed, he added.

 Kevin Tsai says he has never supported Taiwan independence
 2026-10-26 
 EXPLANATION: 
 Tsai said he attended events featuring various interviewees to observe them firsthand as part of his interview research Television host Kevin Tsai (蔡康永) last night broke his silence over a controversy surrounding his appearance at a campaign event for Democratic Progressive Party Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen (沈伯洋), saying he had never supported Taiwan independence.
“I have always hoped for friendly cross-strait relations. I have never supported Taiwan independence,” Tsai wrote in a post on the Chinese social media platform Sina Weibo.
Tsai, who has hosted television shows in China, attended the opening of Shen’s campaign headquarters on Oct. 4, drawing criticism from Chinese social media users and prompting some Chinese companies to distance themselves from him.
